notes: Asserts ready → working → waiting when a tool call opens Copilot's confirmation prompt. UNLIKE every hook-driven sibling, the whole signal is transcript-borne: Copilot writes permission.requested to events.jsonl WHILE it sits blocked (verified live on CLI 1.0.77), the tailer folds requestId into openPermissions (applyPermissionDeltas), TranscriptPermissionPending goes true (tailer_metrics.go:475) and the TierTranscript rule `transcript_permission_prompt` (state_classifier.go:151) routes to waiting — below the hook-tier rules, above agent_done. No hook, no :7837 pinning, and it reproduces under REPLAY (replayengine/metrics.go:136). The recipe never answers the prompt, so final state = waiting, mirroring the claudecode and codex siblings. PRESESSION shape (PROVISIONAL, from the driver+adapter, not a recording): Copilot creates the session-state directory at launch with only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl on the first prompt, so a transient proc-<PID> row is born before the real session (id = the directory name via sessionIDFromPath) reconciles under a DIFFERENT session_id — every post-birth phase anchors to the REAL session. RECORDING PRECONDITION: the driver must launch WITHOUT --allow-all, which pre-approves everything and would suppress the prompt entirely. OBSERVATIONS assert `agent` only: the run terminates mid-turn in waiting, before any assistant.turn_end / session.usage_checkpoint / session.shutdown, and those are the only events carrying Copilot's token block — so cost and tokens are legitimately zero here.
